findings.evidence: <select id="dob-day-select" autocomplete="bday-day" required=""> <select id="dob-month-select" autocomplete="bday-month" required=""> <select id="dob-year-select" autocomplete="bday-year" required="">
findings.fix: Use three short text fields for day, month and year, with the numeric input mode.
findings.violation: A date the person knows by heart is picked from three drop-downs, the year from 60 options.

findings.evidence: <label id="acctnum-label" for="acctnum-input">Account number</label> <input id="acctnum-input" name="account_number" type="text" inputmode="numeric" required> on a form headed "Create your account" whose submit button reads "Create account".
findings.fix: Remove the account-number field from account creation, or, if it links a pre-existing membership, mark it clearly optional and explain why it is being asked for before the account exists.
findings.violation: The task this form performs is creating an account that does not exist yet, so it cannot use an answer that presupposes one already exists; the field asks for information the task has no way to act on.

findings.evidence: <label id="legalname-label" for="legalname-input">Your name</label> <input id="legalname-input" name="legal_name" type="text" autocomplete="name" required> appears after #name-input, <label id="name-label">Full name</label>, which the same form already required.
findings.fix: Remove the duplicate name field, or state in both labels why two different names are needed (for example a legal name distinct from a display name) if that is genuinely the case.
findings.violation: The task is creating an account, and this field asks again for the person's name, which the form already collected under Full name; the account-creation task cannot use two different name answers.

findings.evidence: <label id="member-label" for="member-input">Membership number (8 digits)</label> <input id="member-input" name="membership_number" type="text" inputmode="numeric" placeholder="Must be 8 digits" required> required alongside #acctnum-input on the same account-creation form.
findings.fix: Remove the membership-number requirement from account creation, or move it to a later, clearly optional step for people who are linking an existing membership.
findings.violation: Like the account-number field beside it, this field requires an identifier from a membership that cannot exist before the account being created exists, so the account-creation task has no use for the answer it demands.

findings.evidence: <fieldset id="row-dob"><legend>Date of birth</legend> ... three required selects (day, month, year) ... on a form whose heading is "Create your account" and whose only other fields are name, email, password, address and shipping-related data.
findings.fix: Remove the date-of-birth requirement from account creation, or ask for it only when a later step genuinely needs it (for example age-restricted products), with a stated reason.
findings.violation: Nothing in the form's task, stated as creating an account to buy outdoor gear, uses a date of birth; the form requires it before the account the task creates exists, and never says why.

findings.evidence: <input id="postal-input" name="postal_code" type="text" autocomplete="postal-code" required="" size="3"> (size=3)
findings.fix: Size the field to show at least 5 characters.
findings.violation: This postal code field shows 3 characters, too few to show a typical value whole while it is typed and checked.

findings.fix: Loosen the pattern to accept every valid way of writing the value, and normalise it after submission.
findings.violation: The pattern on this phone field rejects valid values such as +44 20 7946 0958; 020 7946 0958.

findings.evidence: <button id="viewdetails-btn" type="button" style="padding:12px 20px;font-size:16px">View details</button> sits between the #row-contacttime field and the #row-dob fieldset, and carries explicit padding and font-size while the real primary submit, #submit-btn, carries none.
findings.fix: Move the "View details" control outside the field column, for example beside or above the form as a whole, and keep only the primary action in line with the fields where they end.
findings.violation: An action unrelated to finishing the form interrupts the single column of fields, sitting above the date-of-birth fieldset rather than beside the primary action where the fields end, so a person reaching it may believe entry is finished before the remaining required fields.

findings.evidence: #org-input (Organization name), #website-input (Company website), #shipspeed-select (Preferred shipping speed) and #contacttime-input (Preferred contact time) are all required on the same account-creation form, none explained by the heading "Create your account" or the submit label "Create account".
findings.fix: Make these fields optional at sign-up, or move them to the step that actually uses each answer (checkout for shipping speed, a profile page for organization and contact-time preferences).
findings.violation: These four required fields ask for business, logistics and scheduling details that the stated task of creating an account does not need now, and each could wait until a step that actually uses it, such as placing an order or completing a business profile.

findings.evidence: font-size: 13px declared by its inline style
findings.fix: Set the field's font size to at least 16 pixels.
findings.violation: The text in this field is 13 pixels, below the 16 pixels at which a phone stops zooming the page on focus.
This web address field is type text, so a phone does not show the keyboard built for it.

findings.evidence: <label id="contacttime-label" for="contacttime-input" style="display:inline-block;float:left;width:140px">Preferred contact time</label> is the only label in the form whose declared CSS sets a side-by-side position; every other label in the form carries no positioning CSS at all.
findings.fix: Remove the float and fixed width from this label, or, if a beside position is wanted, apply the same position consistently to every label in the form.
findings.violation: The form's one declared label position breaks from the rest of the form's implicit stacked convention, so the label alignment is inconsistent across the form rather than uniform throughout.
